judged_text: The BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS deny-list is lowercased at build time but compared against the raw (non-lowercased) guest input with includes(guest), so any mixed-case variant of a blacklisted address bypasses the block. An operator who blacklists an address (e.g. an abuser or an opted-out party) is defeated by the attacker typing 'Victim@X.com' instead of 'victim@x.com'; the blacklisted party still receives calendar invites/emails, defeating the control this env var exists to provide.

record.issue_text: [BUG] The BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS deny-list is lowercased at build time but compared against the raw (non-lowercased) guest input with includes(guest), so any mixed-case variant of a blacklisted address bypasses the block. An operator who blacklists an address (e.g. an abuser or an opted-out party) is defeated by the attacker typing 'Victim@X.com' instead of 'victim@x.com'; the blacklisted party still receives calendar invites/emails, defeating the control this env var exists to provide.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is normalized to lowercase (`map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but the filter compares it against the raw `guest` string (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`). Since the input schema (`z.string().email()`) does not guarantee lowercase, a mixed-case variant of a blacklisted address would not match and would be allowed, defeating the deny-list and potentially sending invites/emails to blocked addresses.
